q: The dictum “Architecture should appeal to the human heart while also being logical” belongs to.
n: Kenzo Tange said architecture must appeal to the human heart, yet its basic forms and spaces must be logical. Source: Pritzker Prize, Kenzo Tange (1987) acceptance and citation.

q: The dictum "Architecture must create buildings which are conceived as a total artistic expression" belongs to.
n: The idea of buildings conceived as a total artistic expression is attributed to Alvar Aalto's holistic design, from building to furniture. Source: Alvar Aalto Foundation; Schildt, Alvar Aalto.

q: Who said, "Modern architecture need not be Western"?
n: Kenzo Tange argued that "modern architecture need not be Western," fusing Japanese tradition with modernism. Source: Pritzker Prize, Kenzo Tange (1987) materials; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Who said, “Architecture is an inseparable work of art"?
n: Walter Gropius saw architecture as an inseparable union of the arts, the idea behind the Bauhaus "total work of art". Source: Gropius, Bauhaus Manifesto (1919).

q: Which is Kenzo Tange's famous dictum?
o: Modern architecture need not be Western.
n: "Modern architecture need not be Western" is Kenzo Tange's dictum. The others belong to Mies, Venturi and Sullivan. Source: Pritzker Prize, Kenzo Tange (1987).

q: Which is a famous Frank Lloyd Wright dictum?
o: Modern architecture need not be Western.
Less is only more where more is no good.
n: "Less is only more where more is no good" is Frank Lloyd Wright's reply to Mies. Source: Pfeiffer, Frank Lloyd Wright (quotations).

q: Who said form and function should be one, "joined in a spiritual union"?
n: Wright held that form and function should be one, "joined in a spiritual union". Source: Wright, An Autobiography; Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation.

q: “Architecture is organic.”
n: Frank Lloyd Wright championed organic architecture. His organic architecture sought harmony between building, site and occupants. Source: Wright, An Organic Architecture (1939).

q: “Without this spirit, Modernist architecture cannot fully exist. Since there is often a mismatch between the logic and the spirit of Modernism, I use architecture to reconcile the two.”
n: This statement on reconciling the logic and spirit of Modernism is Tadao Ando's. Source: Ando, Pritzker Prize (1995) acceptance and writings.

q: Who wrote, "Nothing requires the architect's care more than the due proportions of buildings"?
n: Vitruvius wrote that nothing requires the architect's care more than the due proportions of buildings. Source: Vitruvius, De Architectura, Book VI.

q: Who said, "Make no little plans; they have no magic to stir men's blood"?
n: "Make no little plans; they have no magic to stir men's blood" is attributed to Daniel Burnham. Source: Moore, Daniel H. Burnham: Architect, Planner of Cities (1921).

q: Who wrote "Architecture or Revolution"?
n: "Architecture or Revolution" is the closing chapter of Le Corbusier's Towards a New Architecture (1923). Source: Le Corbusier, Vers une architecture.

q: “Cube within a cube.”
n: The "cube within a cube" describes Le Corbusier's Purist villas, such as the Villa Savoye's box raised on pilotis. Source: Fondation Le Corbusier; Curtis, Le Corbusier: Ideas and Forms.

q: Who said every great architect is necessarily a great poet and interpreter of his age?
n: Frank Lloyd Wright said every great architect is necessarily a great poet and an interpreter of his age. Source: Wright, writings (quoted in Pfeiffer).

q: Who said architecture must have strength, utility and beauty?
n: Vitruvius held that architecture must have firmitas, utilitas and venustas: strength, utility and beauty. Source: Vitruvius, De Architectura, Book I.

q: “The city must be subject to growth, decay, and renewal."
n: Kenzo Tange's Metabolist-era urbanism held that the city must be subject to growth, decay and renewal. Source: Tange, A Plan for Tokyo (1960); Koolhaas & Obrist, Project Japan.

q: Who argued that only the tomb and the monument belong to art, and everything functional is excluded?
n: Adolf Loos argued that only the tomb and the monument belong to art. Everything that serves a purpose is excluded. Source: Loos, Architecture (1910).

q: “But the building's identity resided in the ornament.”
n: For Louis Sullivan, ornament was integral: a building's identity resided in its organic ornament. Source: Sullivan, A System of Architectural Ornament (1924).

q: Who proclaimed "Art and technology, a new unity" (often quoted with architecture)?
n: Walter Gropius proclaimed "Art and technology, a new unity" at the 1923 Bauhaus exhibition. Source: Bauhaus-Archiv Berlin.

q: “Space is the breath of art”
n: "Space is the breath of art" is attributed to Frank Lloyd Wright. Source: Wright, writings (quoted in Pfeiffer).

q: Who said each architectural project "is like life starting all over again"?
n: Renzo Piano said each project "is like life starting all over again". Source: Pritzker Prize, Renzo Piano (1998) materials.

q: Who said, "An idea is salvation by imagination"?
n: Frank Lloyd Wright said "An idea is salvation by imagination". Source: Wright, writings (quoted in Pfeiffer).

q: Among the color choices, what is not used by Le Corbusier in the Ronchamp Church?
n: Blue is taken here as the colour not used. Ronchamp's palette is dominated by reds, yellows and greens in its painted glass and enamel door, so check photographs, since some panes appear blue-tinted. Source: Fondation Le Corbusier (Notre-Dame du Haut).

q: An architect known for attention to architectural details and the repetition of modular units.
n: Norman Foster is known for precise detailing and repeated modular, often prefabricated, components in High-Tech buildings. Source: Foster + Partners; Pritzker Prize (1999).

q: Which High-Tech landmark has exposed, color-coded service pipes?
n: The Centre Pompidou (Piano and Rogers, 1977) has exposed, colour-coded service pipes (blue air, green water, yellow electrical, red circulation). Source: Centre Pompidou official site.

q: Who designed the Bank of China Tower in Hong Kong?
n: I.M. Pei designed the Bank of China Tower in Hong Kong (1990). The 367 m tower's triangulated frame was inspired by bamboo shoots. Source: Pei Cobb Freed & Partners.
